messages:
jordan_support: Heads up — multiple hosted inference customers are seeing 503s starting ~09:12 UTC. CS is getting a flood of tickets. Topline: 503 gateway errors, some 500s, and spikes in tail latency. :rotating_light:

jordan_support: Observed 15% request failure rate to /v1/generate across eu-west-1. Customer report includes this sample: 
```\nPOST /v1/generate\n{\n  model: \"redwood-xl-7b\",\n  input: \"<~20k token prompt>\"\n}\n```\n
maya_oncall: I see the same on the infra dashboards — host inference routing shows upstream worker restarts for pool gpu-eu-w1. Pod restart count jumped at 09:11.

maya_oncall: k8s events show CrashLoopBackOff for worker-0 and worker-3.

eli_runtime: grabbing logs now. running: `kubectl -n inference logs worker-0 --previous`

eli_runtime: log excerpt: 
```
[2026-05-18T09:11:02Z] runtime: serve request id=abc123
[2026-05-18T09:11:03Z] ERROR: cuda runtime error: out of memory (700) at /workspace/runtime/gpu/kernels.cu:421
[2026-05-18T09:11:03Z] FATAL: segfault (signal 11) at 0x7f9d3a2b
[2026-05-18T09:11:03Z] stack: ... kernelLaunch(...) ...
```

eli_runtime: also seeing `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` in the same timeframe for the other pod.

maya_oncall: Symptoms line up with large prompt lengths + GPU memory pressure. Could be an OOM that escalates to a segfault.

jordan_support: Customers say it happens on long context requests and sometimes under sustained QPS. One customer provided a repro: concatenating multi-megabyte prompt from logs triggers 503s consistently.

tasha_sre: Assigning sev-1. Page DB sec for customers affected list. I'm going to throttle new traffic to the cluster and enable fallback routing to cpu-fallback in eu-west-1.

tasha_sre: Actions in flight:
- cordon node gpu-14 (suspected bad host)
- scale up worker hot pool by +3 on different hosts: `rz scale inference-pool --replicas +3 --region eu-west-1`
- set routing fallback policy: route->cpu-fallback for requests > 4k tokens

eli_runtime: Running `nvidia-smi` snapshot from worker-0 before restart: 
```\n+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+\n| GPU  Name        | Fan | Temp | Memory-Usage | GPU-Util | Processes |\n| 0   A100-40GB    | 21% | 48C  | 40310MiB / 40960MiB | 95% | python (pid 12345) |\n+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+\n```\n
eli_runtime: The worker was at ~98% memory on model load/long prompt. Then we see kernel crash.

maya_oncall: Did we deploy anything risky yesterday?

eli_runtime: There was a runtime build rolled at 03:30 UTC with a small change to attention cache handling. Not yet proven related but marking as suspicious. Build id: build-20260517-rt-7.

deploy-bot: deploy finished: build-20260517-rt-7 promoted to staged @ 03:31 UTC by ci/cd.

tasha_sre: Immediate mitigation: rolling restart to drain pods with heated memory footprint and pin traffic away from the problematic pool. Also reverting runtime build to previous (build-20260516-rt-3) for the eu-west-1 lane.

eli_runtime: Revert command executed: `rz deploy --region eu-west-1 --build build-20260516-rt-3 --force` — rollout started at 09:28 UTC. Monitoring logs for segfaults.

maya_oncall: CS: please update impacted customers with ETA ~30m while we confirm stability and escalate to eng if repeats.

customer_ops_lead: Pushing a note to top 10 customers, offering priority support + 5k credits as a placeholder until we fully quantify impact.

eli_runtime: After revert, observed fewer immediate crashes — restart spikes normalizing. One remaining pod showed `IllegalAddress` at 09:36 and then stabilized.

tasha_sre: Followups for postmortem:
- collect full gcore / coredump from crashed container (we have previous logs but need full dump)
- capture `kubectl describe` + k8s node dmesg for gpu-14
- run stress tests with long-context synthetic prompts to repro locally
- add a guard in routing: refuse requests > 16k tokens for the affected model family until we have a quantized/cached path

eli_runtime: Repro notes so far: long prompts (>=12k tokens) + sustained concurrency >=8 causes memory to grow beyond model KV cache expectations; retention of old KV entries is higher in build-20260517-rt-7 due to a bug in cache eviction which increases peak memory by ~10-15%. That pushes a full A100 over the edge at high QPS.

maya_oncall: Can we implement an emergency rate-limit or token-cost gating on the hosted API while permanent fix is developed?

tasha_sre: Yes — enabling token-based quota checks for the next 4h in eu-west-1 and adding 503->429 transformation for heavy requests so customers get clearer error/suggested backoff.

jordan_support: CS will send the 10-top-customer blast now with the workaround (shorter context / reduce concurrency) and note IDs for follow-up.

eli_runtime: Next steps: reproduce locally, add cache-eviction fix to runtime, test under staged perf, deploy to eu-west-1, then lift gating. Queueing a patch PR and assigning to @eli_runtime.

tasha_sre: Will own post-incident analysis and timeline. Please drop any logs/snippets into the incident doc (link: https://rwd.internal/incidents/1769001234) and tag me.

maya_oncall: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread open for updates. :eyes:
